newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian basketball centre Chris Anstey, 22, is expected to be picked in the late first or early second round of the American National Basketball Association draft to be held in Charlotte, North Carolina, this morning. Page 20.

Three-year-old rivals Marble Halls and Yippyio lead the betting on the Caulfield-Melbourne Cups double. Marble Halls it at 12-1 for the Melbourne Cup and 10-1 for the Caulfield, while Yippyio is at 12-1 for both races. Entries do not close for five weeks,but the Victorian Racing Club has granted rails bookmaker Michael Eskander permission to begin fielding on the races. Page 20.

World short-course swimming champion Natasha Bowron is fighting a recurring abdominal complaint which has forced her out of the water completely, leaving the Australian swimming team without a recognised female distance swimmer for the Pan Pacific champioships in Japan in August. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Rugby League's main financier Optus Vision is believed to have held talks with News Ltd yesterday following the ARL's surprise announcement is would back a new elite competition. ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker said yesterday the ARL has accepted a secondary "State competition" involving all Optus Cup clubs, which infers that not all Optus clubs would be in a future national competition. Page 54.

The Queensland Maroons overcame the loss of two players in the first half of last night's third and final Australian Rugby League State of Origin match to beat the New South Wales Blues 18-12. New South Wales had already won the first two games, giving thm the series 2-1. Page 54.

The New South Wales Trainers' Association has called for radical changes to the future of the state's racing industry, including the amalgamation of the Australian Jockey Club and the Sydney Turf Club, rationalisation of country racing and a freeze on nigt racing until it has proven to be successful interstate. Page 53.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League racial vilification code will be reshaped by the league's administration today, following an Equal Opportunity Commission report that suggested fines be imposed for breaching confidentiality agreements, and that a conciliator should receive written documentation from those involved in any allegation before looking for a resolution to the charge. Page B8.

World soccer body FIFA has suggested to the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games that Melbourne, Canberra, Adelaide and Brisbane host games before the Olympics are opened. But FIFA delegate and Soccer Australia chairman David Hill considers i highly that unlikely the first official soccer games of the Olympics will be played outside Sydney. Page B8.

Brian Cook, chief executive of Australian Football League side West Coast Eagles, has suggested an annual Victoria versus the rest of Australia match as an alternative to the Australian Football League State of Origin, and to keep interstate competition aive. Victorian chairman of selectors Gerard Healy said he did not think the idea would work. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Jockey Brent Stanley's hopes of winning his first apprentices' title are in jeopardy following a fall at Flemington yesterday. Riding River Express in the Tennessee Vain Handicap, Stanley was catapulted from the saddle and then galloped on by Diamond Tiar, but escaped serious injury, suffering only a bruised shoulder which will see him miss three city meetings. Page 86.

Victoria's Australian Football League clubs are considering a proposal they buy a franchise to play their reserve side in the Victorian Football League. The AFL is considering the future of the reserves and looking at a series of options including clubs tking over an existing VFL team. Page 83.

Sky Channel's pay-TV service will see existing race coverage reduced by 35 per cent as part of its move to a "colour and excitement package". Sky chief Warren Wilson said yesterday that Sky pay-TV, which will begin broadcasting within 16 weeks of Sydney'smajor race clubs signing up, will be vastly different from the current format. Page 82.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Parramatta Auburn lost the lead of the New South Wales Dairy Farmers State Netball League last night when they were defeated by Ku-ring-gai 49-47. It was the second consecutive loss for Parramatta Auburn, who started the season with eight straight wins. Page 95.

Australia's elite athletes are having their blood analysed to pick up iron deficiencies which could may lead to oxygen-sapping anaemia. Australian Institute of Sport laboratory manager Robin Parisotto says the testing could provide an Olympic advantage asiron deficiencies deplete oxygen flow to the muscles and would decrease performance. Page 88.

Adelaide Rams rugby league captain Kerrod Walters has warned Perth player Mark Geyer to leave his emotions on the sideline when the teams meet in Geyer's return to the Super League competition this weekend from a ten week suspension. Geyer was suspended for seven weeks for eye-gouging and three weeks for a head-high tackle in the first clash between the teams earlier this season. Page 92.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
